text.text_excerpt: Full disclosure: I attended the monthly dinner of NOLA Eats, and so if this review seems redundant, I apologize in advance. I normally eschew hotel restaurants because they are either too expensive or the execution of the food doesn't justify the expense. La Cote was a pleasant surprise in both areas. First, we were treated to a raw bar appetizer buffet of shrimp, oysters and mussels on the half shell, and for our lone vegetarian, salad. Now, I didn't try the mussels. But the oysters were incredibly fresh. I passed on the shrimp, because you had to peel them. We weren't yet seated for dinner, so this feat wasn't as easy as it seemed. As the restaurant wasn't that busy and the gathering wa...

the food here was surprisingly good, in spite of some reviews i've read elsewhere about this place. talking to one of the staff, i learned that the new chef is looking to reinvent the place, and i think the renaissance has begun (no pun intended). we had a special menu while there, so it may or may not reflect the norm, but it was still delicious. while there, if you get a chance, drop some of the colored salt that comes with the oysters into your water, and see how the wait-staff reacts :-P

Although this is not my first choice for fine dinning in New Orleans, you will not be disappointed in your meal. As the name suggests, their menu is filled with fresh seafood. The servers are very attentive and helpful. And, the bar makes great drinks. Sorry if my review for this restaurant is bland. I guess it's because, although I have nothing but positive things to say about this place, I wasn't blown away. With so many great restaurants in the area with more oomph, I'd reserve La Cote for when you need to take out of town colleagues out for a good meal.
